item.title: Turkish GTA 6 fans want language support so badly that they went out of their way to professionally dub the game's gameplay reveal.
item.description: Turkish GTA 6 fans want language support so badly that they went out of their way to professionally dub its gameplay reveal. The Turkish gaming community has been asking for more and more studios to add Turkish language support for their games. This has led to massive fan campaigns for titles like 007 First Light, which actually resulted in IO Interactive adding Turkish subtitles to the game. Now, the Turkish gaming community is turning their focus to the most anticipated release of the year, if not the most anticipated game in history: Grand Theft Auto 6. Fans have been asking Rockstar Games to add Turkish subtitles or voice overs to GTA 6 ahead of its release in November. They aren't just making social media posts tagging Rockstar, either; they actually professionally dubbed and mixed the entire GTA 6 extended look with a whole cast of actors. The Turkish dub went up just a day after the gameplay was released, which means there was a very fast turn around. It's pretty impressive and shows, there are members of the community actively trying to make this a reality. YouTuber Pintipanda also made a video asking Rockstar to see the potential in localizing GTA 6 for Turkish players. In it, he points out how Turkish-speaking individuals exist in a number of countries outside of Turkey itself, and that GTA 6 is bound to have a wide reach, so it should be as inclusive as possible.

item.title: Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is bringing back a fan-favorite character that tragically died.
item.description: Spoilers for Dexter: Resurrection Season 1 and seemingly Season 2 follow below. Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is bringing back a fan-favorite character that tragically died. Deadline has reported that Angel Batista, played by David Zayas, will return in the next season of Dexter: Resurrection. Batista has been in every single season of Dexter in some form since the very beginning, but he met an unfortunate end in Season 1 of Resurrection. After trying to bring Dexter to justice, he ended up being shot and killed by the season's antagonist, Leon Prater. It was a tragic conclusion to the character's arc and one that punished Dexter for trying to have it all. However, Batista will be back once again in Season 2. The actor was seen on set filming a scene with Michael C. Hall in Times Square. Interestingly, he was sporting a more colorful outfit than the last time we saw him, with a Hawaiian shirt, his signature hat, and his gun holster. This seems to suggest that Zayas is returning as one of Dexter's ghosts, preserved in an outfit from when he was a detective in Florida. Various characters have appeared after their deaths to guide or antagonize Dexter over the course of the franchise, but they're not literal ghosts. They're more like manifestations of Dexter's conscience, so Batista may represent some kind of internal guilt for the titular serial killer this time around.

item.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker already has a time-altering mod that largely defeats the purpose of the game.
item.description: The Blood of Dawnwalker already has a mod that largely defeats the purpose of the game. In The Blood of Dawnwalker, a new RPG from ex-CD Projekt Red staff, the player fills the shoes of a man-turned-vampire who has 30 days to save his family. The game has a non-linear story with different approaches, allowing you to progress how you see fit, but there's a catch: Every mission you take on advances the game's 30-day clock. Some quests advance the clock more than others, forcing the player to be thoughtful about quests they accept. Character progression, such as using the skill tree, also advances the clock. Naturally, some fans don't like the pressure this creates. The clock forces them to make tough decisions; it means you have to be choosey about what you do in the game. With that said, it makes sense that its most popular mod completely removes the tension created by this mechanic. The Better Story Timer mod on NexusMods gives you 90 days to do quests, triple the intended amount. This means you don't really have to be precious about the in-game clock or think too hard about your choices. It removes most, if not all, of the friction in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Of course, something like this might make sense a couple of months post-release for those who want to play it differently, but it literally just came out today. The mod has been downloaded almost 10,000 times already, meaning it's pretty popular... but some users have expressed annoyance over players not giving the game a chance in the way it was intended.

item.title: Netflix is cooking up a live-action Dungeons & Dragons TV show based on the tabletop RPG’s gothic-horror campaign, Ravenloft, and its vampire villain, Darklord Strahd von Zarovich.
item.description: Netflix is cooking up a live-action Dungeons & Dragons TV show based on the tabletop RPG’s gothic-horror campaign, Ravenloft, and its vampire villain, Darklord Strahd von Zarovich. The spooky series is penned as an origin story that dives into the events that turned Zarovitch into the vicious vampire count we all know and love today. As told by Variety, Netflix’s Ravenloft show is described as a “prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance.” “Ravenloft and its Domains of Dread redefine adventure through character-driven stories of dark magic and supernatural intrigue. At the heart of the series, Ravenloft follows the making of the vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovich, whose story of power, love, obsession, and undead transformation charts his origins from tragic antihero to one of Dungeons & Dragons’ most notorious villains,” the description reads.

item.title: There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website. While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly. Could Blizzard be teasing a new StarCraft game?
item.description: There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website. While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly. Could Blizzard be teasing a new StarCraft game? That would make sense. A report earlier this year said that Blizzard had partnered with Korean gaming giant Nexon to develop a new StarCraft shooter. Blizzard declined to comment on the matter at the time, and the partnership remains unconfirmed, but a report yesterday from South Korean newspaper Chosun (via Wccftech) reaffirms that Nexon is seeking a license to develop a new StarCraft game. Meanwhile, Blizzard may have been working on its own new StarCraft game, as per a 2024 job posting for an "upcoming open-world shooter." Reports from that time suggested the title was in development at Blizzard, led by former Far Cry executive producer Dan Hay, who joined the company in 2022. Another point of evidence is that BlizzCon returns on September 12 after a three-year hiatus, and Blizzard will undoubtedly want to make a splash there with big news beyond its ongoing franchises. There's also a conspicuous hour-long gap on BlizzCon's day-one mainstage programming, while all other panels only have 15 minutes of downtime between them. Sure seems like the place for something that gets announced during the opening ceremonies.

item.title: The directors of Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, admitted the fantasy flick flopped due to “not-so-great timing” because of The Super Mario Bros. movie and drama with Wizards of the Coast’s proposed D&D licensing changes.
item.description: The directors of Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, admitted the fantasy flick flopped due to “not-so-great timing” because of The Super Mario Bros. movie and drama with Wizards of the Coast’s proposed D&D licensing changes. Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves released in March 2023, right around the time that Wizards of the Coast was facing massive backlash from players after confirming planned adjustments to their Open-Gaming License that would have made sweeping changes to rules that allowed creators to make and sell their own content based on the tabletop RPG’s fifth edition. While they ultimately ended up walking this disastrous decision back, the blowback was enough to negatively impact the movie adaptation, says director John Francis Daley. He claims that this drama, alongside the hugely-successful launch of The Super Mario Bros. Movie around the same time, ultimately overshadowed a film that has since proven to be a hit among fans after the fact. “It was very much a product of not-so-great timing when the first movie came out,” Daley said in an episode of The Discourse Podcast. “It came out four days before the Super Mario movie, which broke records. It came out a month after Wizards of the Coast changed the official gaming license, prompting many D&D fans to boycott the game, and I don’t think the marketing did enough to tell people who weren’t already fans that this movie might be for them. Yeah, so it was a perfect storm of all of those elements, and we’ll see.”

item.title: The Sheriff of Miami-Dade county is speaking out against Miami’s proposal to celebrate the launch of GTA 6 by decking out the city in advertisements for the highly-anticipated game, arguing that it glorifies crime and undermines the efforts of law enforcement.
item.description: The Sheriff of Miami-Dade county is speaking out against Miami’s proposal to celebrate the launch of GTA 6 by decking out the city in advertisements for the highly-anticipated game, arguing that it glorifies crime and undermines the efforts of law enforcement. Grand Theft Auto 6 takes place in Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, Florida. Rockstar took pains to faithfully recreate Miami’s most iconic locales and architecture within the game, with fans already spotting a few real-life locations in the title’s newest trailers. In late August, local news outlets reported that Miami-Dade County officials had spoken with Rockstar Games about potential plans for a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed takeover of Miami, which included ideas like wrapping the Metro line with Vice City branding, creating Vice City manhole covers, and decking out the Miami International Airport with ‘Welcome to Vice City’ signage. While nothing has been formally approved, it seemed like the city was gung-ho for a partnership with the biggest game of the year… but now, the Miami-Dade county sheriff is bringing those ideas to a screeching halt.

Since revealing his new relationship with Hollywood, Brandon Sanderson's weekly podcast has become increasingly focused on movie and book adaptations. This week, he and his co-host Dan Wells dove into the topic of the Project Hail Mary movie, and Sanderson makes a compelling case for reading Andy Weir's book. "They left out a lot of the science, the try fails, the figuring out how everything works," Sanderson said. He went on to explain that the moment he finds out he's on a spaceship is quite a bit longer in the books compared to the movie, describing the experience as if "you're figuring it out with him, like what is this? What is going on?" Sanderson still had nothing but positive things to say about the film, saying he thinks "they did a fantastic job." IGN's review of the film reflects his same sentiment, which landed it on our list of the top-reviewed movies of 2026 so far. "Thrilling, heartfelt, and hilarious, Project Hail Mary is a rollicking sci-fi blockbuster. Lord and Miller faithfully adapt Andy Weir’s novel, carrying forward the author’s celebration of science, teamwork, and bravery on a huge scale, bolstered by great performances from Ryan Gosling and James Ortiz and Greig Fraser’s fantastic work behind the camera. Some pacing issues inherent in closely adapting the novel’s structure do make for a somewhat rough landing, but through the lens of Grace and Rocky’s partnership being the real mission we want to see succeed, Project Hail Mary is a memorable celebration of how much we can accomplish when we work together." - Tom Jorgensen

item.title: Not content just to appear in Marvel's X-Men reboot, Inde Navarrette has signed on to star in a bizarre sci-fi thriller called The Waffle House Index.
item.description: Obsession star Inde Navarrette may have just signed on for Marvel's upcoming X-Men reboot, but that's not stopping her from taking on smaller and weirder projects. Case in point: Navarrette is slated to star in The Waffle House Index, a sci-fi thriller about a Waffle House waitress dealing with an overnight shift from hell. The news comes courtesy of The Hollywood Reporter. THR writes that the film has just been picked up by Apple Original Films. It features a screenplay by Andrew Nunnelly, one that was featured on the 2025 Black List (a list of the most acclaimed unproduced scripts circulating in Hollywood). The Waffle House Index is slated to be directed by Louis Paxton (The Incomer). The film will be produced by Plan B Entertainment, with Navarrette herself executive producing. The title of the film refers to the infamous barometer Waffle House restaurants use while under hurricane threat. A Waffle House Index can range from green to yellow to red depending on how severe weather conditions are and whether a given restaurant stays open or not. In short, if the Waffle House Index is red, it's time to panic. The index may well reach the red zone in this movie, as it's teased that Navarrette's beleaguered character will deal with everything from a rogue gunman to flash floods to crocodile attacks to nuclear missiles and even a hidden bunker located underneath the Waffle House itself (hey, it is a sci-fi movie).

item.title: YouTube star Charlie ‘MoistCr1tikal’ White is the mastermind behind a full-length animated movie adaptation of his very own comic, Godslap, set to release in theaters in 2028.
item.description: YouTube star Charles ‘MoistCr1TiKaL’ White is the mastermind behind a full-length animated movie adaptation of his very own comic, Godslap, set to release in theaters in 2028. The film’s first teaser trailer was published on September 3, 2026, showing off the slick animation and smooth artwork from Powerhouse Animation, best known for its work on Netflix’s Castlevania: Nocturne and Masters of the Universe: Revelation. As told by White in a YouTube video announcing the news, the Godslap movie follows Aius, a young man with the “incredibly strong gift of slapping.” However, his incredible power has made his father, Darius, extremely overprotective of him, fearing what could happen if he were to venture into the outside world. First teaser for ‘GODSLAP’, a new animated film based on MoistCr1TiKaL's comic series.The film follows a boy with an extraordinary slapping ability who ventures out into the world for the first time. pic.twitter.com/RfrajR1SuY

item.title: AdHoc Studio, the team behind Disptached, helped develop Until Dawn 2.
item.description: AdHoc Studio, the team behind Disptach, helped develop Until Dawn 2. In a new PlayStation Blog post, Until Dawn 2 developer Firesprite confirmed that AdHoc helped craft the story of the new horror game. As a result, the team promises a much richer experience with tough choices that impact the branching narrative. "We’ve partnered with our friends at AdHoc Studio – the brilliant minds behind the acclaimed Dispatch – so you can expect a deeply layered story packed with rich characters, razor-sharp dialogue, fraught relationships, tough decisions, and yes… more than a few gruesome deaths," reads the post. "Every choice, every interaction can ripple with dramatic consequences." AdHoc has been around for nearly a decade, but only released its first game last year. The team is largely comprised of ex-Telltale, Ubisoft, and Night School Studio talent, which has allowed them to use their narrative expertise for new titles like Dispatch. The 2025 superhero game was a refreshing experience take on a tried and true genre with nuanced relationships, hilarious and compelling writing, and meaningful choices.

item.title: Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann says that neither he nor the studio are involved with the third season of the HBO TV adaptation of the beloved video game, but says that the developer "isn't done" with the franchise yet.
item.description: Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann says that neither he nor the studio are involved with the third season of the HBO TV adaptation of the beloved video game, but says that the developer "isn't done" with the franchise yet. Speaking to The Washington Post, Druckmann said, "I wasn't involved in shaping this season's creative direction, and Naughty Dog did not have a creative role in the direction of this season. So I can't personally speak to how production is progressing." He then pretty clearly suggested that Naughty Dog will take on future projects in The Last of Us universe, though whether that's a proper The Last of Us Part 3, a resurrection of the canceled The Last of Us Online multiplayer project, or something else remains to be seen. "It's important for us to note that as the creator of the games, Naughty Dog is still the steward of this IP and even though this might be the end of this adaptation," he added, referring to the HBO show's third season, "we're not done with The Last of Us. There's a couple projects in the works that, when the time is right, I'm very excited to talk about." Naughty Dog is currently focused on its next game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, which was a no-show at today's Sony State of Play, but did recently wrap cinematic shooting. It does not yet have a release window. On The Last of Us TV show, meanwhile, Peter Sarsgaard has been cast in a role for an original character not featured in the games, while Li Jun Li was cast as Miriam, among numerous other cast announcements. We also recently learned that Matthew McConaughey turned down the part of Joel, which of course went to Pedro Pascal.

item.title: Supergirl officially has a streaming release date.
item.description: Supergirl officially has a streaming release date. The latest movie from James Gunn’s DC reboot will be available to HBO Max subscribers starting next Thursday, September 10. An ASL Version of the film will be available at the same time, and it will debut on HBO linear the following day, September 11, at 8pm ET. Starring Milly Alcock in the titular role, Supergirl is the second major movie in the new DC Universe helmed by James Gunn, following up on last year’s Superman. Unfortunately, it struggled to match its predecessor’s run at the box office. Where Superman quickly soared to over $600 million globally, Supergirl struggled from its opening weekend. The film ended its run in theaters with a worldwide gross of just over $126 million on a budget Variety reported as somewhere between $170 and $185 million.

item.title: Dave Bautista has posted a new video showing his body transformation for Kratos in the new God of War TV series.
item.description: Dave Bautista has posted a new video showing his body transformation for Kratos in the new God of War TV show. Bautista was officially cast as Kratos in the God of War TV series last month and he has wasted no time prepping for the role. The actor shared a video on Instagram flexing his new physique, noting that he has been weight training for three weeks and has two months to "get to where he needs to be." Unlike other roles where an actor might have six to twelve months or more to prepare, Bautista has to hit the ground running. The God of War TV series began shooting earlier this year with actor Ryan Hurst in the role of Kratos. Unfortunately, Hurst got injured (after also putting in the work at the gym for the role) and will be out of commission until next year. Amazon made the decision to recast the role and quickly hired Dave Bautista, who now has just a couple of months to get into Kratos-level shape. The show is expected to restart production in October, meaning Bautista won't have much time to rest. The actor had recently lost a ton of weight and muscle after years of starring in action movies and being a professional wrestler. While Bautsita made sense as Kratos five years ago, some began to question if he was the right choice due to him being much slimmer. Bautista seems to be interested in proving the naysayers wrong and is hitting the weight room to get real beefy before stepping into the shoes of a gaming god.

item.title: If you have yet to see the Odyssey in IMAX 70MM or need an excuse to watch it again, showtimes for Christopher Nolan's epic at 39 theaters worldwide that support the much-desired format have been extended through September 30, 2026.
item.description: If you have yet to see the Odyssey in IMAX 70MM or need an excuse to watch it again, showtimes for Christopher Nolan's epic at 39 theaters worldwide that support the much-desired format have been extended through September 30, 2026. The Odyssey's historic IMAX run was supposed to end on September 15, but the "overwhelming public demand" behind this decision will now see the film staying in the format it's "intended" to be seen for 11 weeks. If you want to see it for yourself, check out the showtimes right here. Since it first premiered on July 17, The Odyssey has become the highest-grossing IMAX release of all time, earning $457 million at the global box office. The IMAX 70MM screenings alone have accounted for $66 million of that across the 41 theaters that feature it. These accolades are fitting, as The Odyssey was also the first film to ever be shot entirely with IMAX cameras.

item.title: Microsoft has announced big changes to Xbox cloud gaming, including a switch to monthly hour limits.
item.description: Microsoft has announced big changes to Xbox cloud gaming, including a switch to monthly hour limits. From November, Game Pass plans will include a set number of cloud gaming hours each month: Once subscribers use their included hours, they can buy additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store. Currently, Game Pass subscribers can stream without these monthly hour limits. The change means those who use cloud gaming most via Game Pass will end up having to pay more, although Microsoft said this impacts 4% of Game Pass subscribers. Also in November, Microsoft said players will be able to buy cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and ‘stream eligible games they own on supported devices’ without subscribing to Game Pass.

Spooky season is just around the corner, and one of the latest LEGO Halloween sets is already getting a discount. Walmart's Bricktember Sale is bringing the first price cut on the hauntingly twisted Mayor Manor set today. Mayor Manor is part of a new line of creepy sets called the Midnight Valley Collection. It's basically a haunted house with oddly angled architecture and glow-in-the-dark minifigures. Seeing as it just came out on September 1, the fact that it's already getting a discount at Walmart is a very welcome surprise. I am personally a big fan of LEGO's Architecture line of sets, so this particular build really appeals to me. Mostly because of the amount of thought that seems to have gone into making it feel haunted. LEGO bricks, by design, are usually perfectly aligned with each other. But the Mayor Manor utilizes its bricks in such a way that everything looks just a little bit crooked. It gives the mansion a rather haunted look without having to resort to things like boarded up windows or a crumbling façade. The Mayor Manor is also designated as an 18+ set, so it's meant for adults to build and display. At just over 1,400 pieces, it's decently sized and comes with a ton of little details inside and outside of the house. In addition to the spooky exterior, you get to build the gothic decor of the inside of the home as well. All-in-all, it's an excellent display piece for Halloween with some cool surprises for anone who gets to build it. You also get three glow-in-the-dark minifigures, a cat, and a rat that you can display anywhere on the set.

item.title: After years of poking fun at Green Lantern, Ryan Reynolds admitted he owes his career and personal life to the infamous 2011 DC superhero movie.
item.description: Ryan Reynolds has spent over a decade mocking his notorious 2011 comic book movie flop, Green Lantern, perhaps most famously by including a meta post-credits scene in Deadpool 2 where the merc with a mouth goes back in time to blow out Reynolds’ brains all over a copy of the Green Lantern screenplay. Now, with the HBO series Lanterns out, the actor seems to have developed an appreciation for his DC film, declaring, “I owe my entire career to that movie.” Speaking on the red carpet at the premiere of his new movie Mayday, Reynolds was asked by Entertainment Tonight if he’d ever consider making a cameo in Lanterns. "I would totally do a cameo in that," Reynolds said. "I love it. I learned so much making that movie. And I know what you're thinking, you're thinking, 'Oh, learned what not to do.' In part, yes. But also, any time you're making something that large, there are core lessons that come of it.” “I owe my entire career to that movie. I owe everything to that,” Reynolds said. “Everything about it was a gift that keeps on giving. And I really enjoyed the experience of making it."

item.title: Takashi Iizuka, a key figure in Sega’s Sonic Franchise, told IGN’s Jeffrey Vega about the unique difficulty the company faced in giving the Blue Blur a playable skin in Fortnite.
item.description: Takashi Iizuka, a key figure in Sega’s Sonic Franchise, told IGN’s Jeffrey Vega about the unique difficulty the company faced in giving the Blue Blur a playable skin in Fortnite. While Shadow is somewhat famous for being an edgy, pistol-toting anti-hero, Sonic is a totally different character. The yang to Shadow’s yin, Sonic is an upbeat hedgehog who uses his extremely fast speed (and occasionally, the power of the Chaos Emeralds) to take down enemies. That’s why Sega balked when it was first approached by Epic games with the idea of giving Shadow and Sonic their own Fortnite skins, according to Sonic Creative Officer Takashi Iizuka. Luckily, they were able to come up with a creative solution: Why not make a new Sonic variant? “Epic Games came and spoke with us a couple years ago about putting Sonic in Fortnite, but Sonic is a character that will never hold a gun,” he told us. “And when thinking about the design of Fortnite, it was really hard to think about Sonic being in the game. But this time, we were able to take creative liberties and created Android Sonic.”

item.title: A former Rockstar Games developer has revealed that the team thought GTA Online was going to fail before it launched.
item.description: A former Rockstar Games developer has revealed that the team thought GTA Online was going to fail before it launched. In an interview with Eldorado, ex-Rockstar Games developer Matt Freedman looked back on the success of GTA 5 and attributed a lot of it to GTA Online. He noted that a lot of investors seek a GTA Online-level success nowadays, but said it was treated as an "afterthought" during its initial development. "When we were working on GTA Online, it was an afterthought," said Freedman. "We were all positive it was going to fail. Everyone thought this thing was going to fail. I remember QA testers coming up to me [and saying], 'We’ve got four hours of content for online mode. To do everything in GTA Online, it’s four hours,' or it was something like that. It was really short, and they’re like: ‘We are in so much trouble,' and we’re all sitting there going, 'Let’s see what happens. We’re going to do our best job anyways.' And then it took off, and then there was, to Rockstar’s credit, a fast follow with as much content as possible and [it] just kind of keep it going. And now it’s become this phenomenon." It's unclear when the perception of GTA Online's potential began to shift at Rockstar. The studio did seem to have ambitions for it before launch, as it released a sizable trailer and media previews for the online mode before the game's release with plans for post-launch content like heists. Still, Freedman is right that the game was pretty light on content upon arrival. There wasn't a ton to do beyond the typical sandbox mayhem and the most exciting content in the game didn't arrive until years later, including its heists update.
